summary: The candidate is correct as stated. The accepted atlas construction and synchronized-label thinning provide an exact parent-label map whose same-parity parent edges imply a(sigma) congruent to z(sigma) congruent to b(sigma) modulo 2; combining this with the same-parity fresh edges proves that both J atom bases are integral. The endpoint allocations and labelwise transportation couplings give the claimed half-scaled label masses, exact repeated-use accounting, zeta_k at most omega_k^b, and total physical use P_cap. The target and source density ledgers remain pointwise admissible after all collisions and repeated tags are aggregated, so both atomic measures are halfspace-dominated and have the stated masses and common first moment. The pooled metronoid memberships, rank-at-most-two complete-core bound, and two separate dominated-measure residual bounds follow with the stated scopes. The Hall cut condition is both necessary and sufficient for the proportional edge-use realization, including zero-demand vertices, and the scaled KKT cancellations and strict normalized affine-defect bound follow exactly from positive homogeneity and the accepted defect inequalities.
